title: agent-fs deployment diagram
description: How afs runs: one binary installed on the machine where its user works, started as a short-lived process per `afs call`, or as a long-lived process per session by a shell (`afs jsonl`) or by an MCP client (`afs serve`). It reads the local file system with the running user's permissions and talks to nothing over a network.

nodes.name: User's machine
nodes.description: A Mac or a Linux machine where the developer works and the agent runs; afs is on its PATH.

nodes.name: afs process
nodes.description: One process per `afs call` (no session memory), or one per session for `afs jsonl` and `afs serve`, holding that session's state in memory until stdin closes.

nodes.name: Terminal or script
nodes.description: A shell in which the developer, or a script, runs `afs call` or `afs jsonl`.

nodes.name: MCP client
nodes.description: The coding agent's MCP client (such as Claude Code with an .mcp.json entry running `afs serve`), which starts afs and keeps it for the session.

artifacts.name: afs
artifacts.description: The release build of the crate (`cargo build --release -p agent-fs` on Linux or macOS), or the universal macOS binary from the release tarball, which the zazzle Homebrew formula installs with the other tools.

relationships.description: Runs as the user who started it.
The developer's shell on the same machine.
The MCP client runs on the same machine and starts afs as its child process.
Command-line arguments and stdin; replies on stdout, one JSON line each, and the exit code.
Starts `afs serve` and speaks MCP (newline-delimited JSON-RPC) over its stdin and stdout.
